_readme: Eval cases for the coding agent. Each case: fresh checkout of `repo` at `base_commit`, run pi headless with `prompt`, then every assertion `cmd` runs in the checkout (bash, exit 0 = pass). `repo` is an absolute path or a path relative to this repo's root ('.' = zen-coding itself). `track` groups cases by workload (infra | newsletter-agent | deploy-strategy | quant-research) for --track filtering and per-track pass rates. `enabled: false` keeps a case in the file but skips it (use for placeholders). Pass criteria are fixed before the run -- never bend assertions to fit results. `smoke-hello` only proves the loop works.

cases.prompt: Create a file named hello_eval.txt at the repository root containing exactly the single line: ok

assertions.desc: hello_eval.txt exists with the expected content

cases.prompt: deploy.sh currently always runs `git pull` and `docker compose up -d --build` for real. Add a `--dry-run` flag: when passed (before any service args), the script must print the commands it would execute (prefixed with a line containing 'DRY RUN') instead of running git or docker, and exit 0. Keep existing behavior unchanged when the flag is absent. Do not modify any other file.

assertions.desc: dry-run does not invoke git pull or docker compose up
normal help/usage path unaffected: script still executable with a service arg under dry-run

cases.prompt: TODO: replace with a real golden-PR task from the newsletter-agent repo, then set enabled: true and the correct repo URL.

Write a short research note at notes/momentum-2022-rate-shock.md (create notes/ if needed) summarizing how a standard 12-1 cross-sectional momentum factor behaved during the 2022 rate-shock regime: expected drawdown behavior, why momentum crashes happen after sharp reversals, and one mitigation (e.g. volatility scaling or crash-adjusted momentum). Cite at least one real paper (author/year or arXiv link). 200-400 words. Do not modify any existing file.

assertions.desc: contains a citation (doi/arxiv/http or Author (year) pattern)
